text:
incidents-bot: P0 alert: increased 5xx rate in eu-west canary cohort (service=redwood-api, route=/v1/generate). Alert fired at 23:12 UTC. @pagerduty paged oncall.

pagerduty: Pager triggered to oncall: jordan.

jordan: Ack. Investigating. seeing a spike from eu-west between 23:11-23:12, error class AuthenticationError in logs.

maya: I'm around, jumping in. Do we have a deploy/rollout in eu-west right now?

jordan: Yes — automated blue/green rollout started ~23:00 for conf-service v3.4.1 -> v3.5.0. Canary weight should be 5% but dashboard shows 25% for eu-west-1 and 0% for eu-west-2, which is odd.

luke: I rolled the canary earlier in eu-west-2. CI triggered routemgr job to shift weights. Looking at route-change logs now.

olivia: Customers on EU may see auth failures and higher latency. Support is getting tickets. tagging support-team.

support-team: Confirmed ~10 customer reports in last 10m. All from EU. Some mention 401s right away.

jordan: Hypothesis: partial DNS/edge config propagation + routemgr retry caused a weight race — some gateways routed traffic to a broken v3.5 instance. Need to pin traffic back to v3.4 ASAP.

maya: Agreed. Two parallel mitigations: 1) feature/kill switch for new auth path, 2) immediate rollback of canary weights to 0 for v3.5 in eu-west.

luke: I can run the weight-set. Executing:

```sh
# set canary weight to 0 for eu-west region
routemgr set-weight --service conf-service --region eu-west --version v3.5.0 --weight 0
```

luke: Command returned OK, but config API shows eu-west-1 still at 20% for v3.5, eu-west-2 at 0%.

jordan: Hmm. Could be caching at the edge / DNS TTL. Check edge cache invalidation and dns propagation.

maya: Running edge cache purge:

```sh
edgectl purge --prefix /v1/generate --regions eu-west --sync
```

maya: Purge ack from endpoints.

olivia: Noted: we should also toggle the feature flag that enables the new auth flow to prevent further hits if traffic still lands on v3.5. Feature flag id: auth_v2_rollout.

luke: I can toggle. Running: 

```sh
ff-toggle --service conf-service --flag auth_v2_rollout --state off --reason "emergency rollback - 5xxs in eu-west"
```

luke: Toggle acknowledged by launchpad: auth_v2_rollout -> off.

support-team: Seeing immediate drop in error reports from some customers. But dashboards still show a 5xx tail in eu-west-1.

jordan: Check origin logs for container restarts / OOMs on v3.5?

luke: Looking at kube: some pods running v3.5 in eu-west-1 are crashlooping with stacktrace referencing new token parsing code. Not load-related.

maya: Given crashes, we should also scale down the faulty deployment and scale up v3.4 replicas.

jordan: Rollback plan: 
1) scale v3.5 -> 0 in eu-west clusters
2) ensure v3.4 healthy replicas restored
3) verify route weights are only to v3.4
4) confirm with dashboards + customer support

luke: Executing step 1:

```sh
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/conf-service-v3-5 --replicas=0 --context=eu-west-1
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/conf-service-v3-5 --replicas=0 --context=eu-west-2
```

luke: Scale commands returned success. Pods terminating.

maya: Step 2: ensure v3.4 scaled to desired: 

```sh
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/conf-service-v3-4 --replicas=12 --context=eu-west-1
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/conf-service-v3-4 --replicas=8 --context=eu-west-2
```

maya: v3.4 pods are coming up healthy (readiness pass).

jordan: Step 3: verify route weights:

```sh
routemgr get-weights --service conf-service --region eu-west
# expected v3.4:100 v3.5:0
```

jordan: get-weights shows v3.4:100% now across both eu-west clusters. Good.

olivia: Support reporting customer reports decreased significantly, some customers still see stale 401s — likely client-side caching or DNS TTL. Any ETA on full recovery?

maya: Edge caches purged and feature flag off. DNS TTL could be up to 60s; we should see tail disappear within 2-3 minutes. Also suggest posting a short status note to customers via status.redwood.ai if we don't reach clear within 10m.

support-team: I'll draft a brief: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in EU due to a partial canary deployment; mitigation in progress; more updates in 10 min."

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-327. Severity: P0. Links: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2025-327

jordan: I'm handing off to maya — I've hit my paging rotation limit for the hour. Maya, you take lead?

maya: I have it. Acknowledge takeover. I'll keep the incident commander role.

olivia: Any customer-impact windows to share to PM/ops? We should quantify affected requests.

maya: Early ballpark: ~2.3% of EU traffic in 23:10-23:20 window, error rate peaked at 8% for the canary cohort. I'll pull precise numbers.

luke: I'll open a PR to add server-side guardrails to prevent parsing exception from bringing down the process (circuit-breaker around token parse).

jordan: Good. After stabilization, we'll run a postmortem focusing on: rollout orchestration resilience, routemgr idempotency, and DNS/edge propagation safety.

maya: Last checks: dashboards show 5xx back to baseline for eu-west at 23:25 UTC. Customer reports down to zero. Marking mitigation complete, keeping incident open for postmortem.

support-team: Notifying customers who opened tickets with the temporary mitigation note.

olivia: Thanks everyone. Quick runbook updates to consider: require canary health gating across all region clusters before weight increases, and add explicit verification that routemgr returned consistent state per-region.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2025-327 status -> mitigated at 23:25 UTC. Next: assign postmortem owner.

maya: I will own the postmortem. I'll include timeline, RCA, and action items. Planning doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incident/INC-2025-327-pm

jordan: Thanks team. Off to rotation.

maya: Closing on-call handover notes and creating JIRA for the guardrail work.

support-team: Closing customer tickets with mitigation note. Will reopen if any new reports. :thumbsup:
